description: Horner nested-rotate WTF1 (value-identical): fold the 8 rotated s_MT0 lookups into a serial rotr-by-8 chain to cut transient live regs and lift occupancy (ncu: register-limited, 1 block/SM, 16.67%, shared allows 2). Neutral: 1544.3 vs 1545.6 best (-0.08%, within noise); selftest PASS. Compiler already balances regs/ILP; single-table win spent, 56 rotates/round fundamental.

Hoist loop-invariant round-1 (-a3): only w[0]=>W0 varies in the bruteforce loop, so precompute the round-1 MDS column contributions of W1..W7 once per thread (run round 1 with S0=0, fold out the spurious Zk=MTk[0]=ROTR64(MT0[0],8k) term via XOR-linearity), leaving 8 lookups/candidate for round 1 instead of 64. Correct (selftest PASS, confirms algebra). 1554.5 vs 1545.6 best = +0.58%, within the 1-2% noise band -> discard. Round-1 shared loads are not the dominant cost; register pressure from base[8]+W1..3,W7 held across the loop offsets the ~8.75% fewer loads. Kernel behaves latency/occupancy-bound (1 block/SM), not shared-throughput-bound.

Skip dead final-round words: COMPARE_*_SIMD consumes only the first 128 bits (D0,D1), so the 10th MixRows round needs only S0,S1 -- computing L2..L7->S2..S7->D2..D7 (6 of 8 WTF1, 48 of 640 shared lookups) is provably dead work. Value-identical for the observable compare; selftest PASS. 1551.6 vs 1545.6 best = +0.39%, within the 1-2% noise band -> discard. Confirms NVRTC already DCEs the unused final-round outputs (SROA of the local dgst[16] array after inlining); making it explicit gains nothing measurable. Whirlpool a3 stays register/occupancy-bound (1 block/SM), not lookup-count-bound.

8-table revert (keep zerokey, drop single-table): WTF1 now indexes 8 distinct shared tables s_MT0..s_MT7 directly instead of 1 table + 56 rotr64/round (MTk[x]==ROTR64(MT0[x],8k); value-identical, MT1..7 are the exact tables the generic transform uses; selftest PASS). Rationale: profile is register-limited (1 block/SM, 16.67%), so single-table shared savings buy no occupancy while costing ~560 rotate ops over 10 rounds; both forms issue the same 64 shared loads/round. Paired same-session median-of-3: baseline single-table 1551.9/1551.9 vs 8-table 1574.9/1576.8, zero overlap, +1.55% (within-condition noise <0.2%). keep.

Roll the fully-unrolled 10-round loop into a #pragma-unroll-1 loop with round keys moved to a CONSTANT_VK rk06100[80] array, to cut register pressure and lift occupancy (measured HEAD 8-table = REG:188 m04, 1 block/SM, 16.67%, register-limited). Correct (value-identical: same rounds/order/keys; selftest PASS). Rolling DID slash registers 188->79 (m04), enough for 2-3 blocks/SM, yet primary dropped 1351.9 vs 1576.8 best = -14.3%, far beyond noise -> discard. Decisive negative result: the kernel is ILP/latency-bound WITHIN each warp, not occupancy-limited -- the full unroll exposes cross-round instruction-level parallelism that hides shared-load latency; #pragma-unroll-1 serializes the 10 rounds (shared loads on the critical path) and the extra occupancy cannot compensate. Confirms register reduction via rolling is counterproductive here; the 8-table full-unroll stays best.

Pre-scaled byte-offset MixRows lookup: replace BOX64(s_MTk, v8x_from_v64(v)) with byte-addressed load BOXO(s_MTk, OFF_x(v)) where OFF_x(v)=((lo/hi 32-bit half)>>(bitpos-3))&0x7f8 computes the byte*8 table offset directly, folding the u64-stride x8 scale (IMAD.SHL) into the extract shift. SASS showed the (extract; index) form emits 3 serial address-calc ops (SHF/IMAD.SHL/LOP3) per lookup on the latency-bound round-to-round critical path; this cuts it to SHF+LOP3 (2 ops). Value-identical (byte j of v -> s_MTk[j]; selftest PASS confirms the mapping). 1579.6 vs 1576.8 best = +0.18%, within the 1-2% noise band -> discard. ptxas already schedules/fuses the x8 scale off the critical path in the real full-unroll build, so the saving seen in the stale cubin does not materialize. 8-table full-unroll stays best; address-path instruction selection is exhausted (mode near roofline).
